items.title: About
items.content:
We study how salt marshes keep up with the sea

Tidewater Lab is a sample research group. We measure how marsh plants, mud and tides work together, and what that means for the towns behind them.

14
field sites

Research interests

  • How fast marshes build elevation
  • Which plants hold sediment best
  • Low-cost sensors for tide and salinity

News

  • Spring: two new field sites join the elevation survey
  • Winter: the sensor design is published as an open kit
  • Fall: three students present at the regional meeting

items.title: Marsh elevation survey
items.content:
Twice a year we measure the height of the marsh surface at fourteen sites and compare it with the tide record.

What we have found

Most sites are keeping up. The ones that are not have lost their tall grass at the water edge.

items.title: Open sensor kit
items.content:
Commercial tide gauges cost more than most classrooms can spend. Ours is built from parts a hardware store carries.

What is in the kit

  • A pressure sensor and a salinity probe
  • A logger that runs for a season on one battery
  • Build notes and the code

items.title: Plants that hold mud
items.content:
We plant test plots with four species and weigh what each plot catches over a year.

Why it matters

Restoration projects choose plants by price and habit. This gives them a third thing to weigh.
